motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the group of items passed together in one vote. The record here does not list which items were in the group.
motions.impact: With no list of items in the record, nothing here names a street, a fee, or a property. Nobody needs to do anything.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New easement rules added to the land use code
motions.summary: The city added a new easements chapter to its land use code and updated the code's definitions to match.
motions.impact: This mainly touches property owners and developers dealing with easements, the strips of land set aside for things like utilities or access. Most residents will see no change day to day.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Facilities Master Plan.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, accepting the Galloway report as a guideline for future adoption of the Eagle Mountain City Facilities Master Plan. The motion died for a lack of a second.
motions.headline: Facilities master plan left unsettled
motions.summary: A proposal to treat the Galloway report as a guide toward a future city facilities master plan drew no support, and the council took no action on it.
motions.impact: How the city plans its buildings for the years ahead stays undecided. Nothing shifts for residents unless the council picks the question back up.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Public Art Plan.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Public Art Plan. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Public art plan adopted
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain adopted a public art plan, the city's written guide for art in public spaces. No money was attached to the motion.
motions.impact: The plan by itself buys nothing and commissions nothing. City staff and anyone proposing public art now have a document to work from; the rest of the city sees no change.

motions.item_title: Add a review of Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones to the Legislativ…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to add a review of Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Residential zoning rules queued for review
motions.summary: The council queued Chapter 17.25, the city's residential zoning rules, for a future review, without changing anything in the rules themselves.
motions.impact: Nothing about what you can build on your lot changes today. If the review produces edits, they would come back to the council before taking effect.
